title: Screen P112 tetrad coefficient fusion under relaxed rank ceilings
body:
## Change and mathematical scope

This is a bounded, source-bound audit of the P112 tetrad consumer under relaxed rank ceilings. It derives a hybrid centre-cut reader and dirty-baseline correction, then compares installing the consumer before canonical phase `B` with exact inverse-transpose retiming after `B`.

For each of fourteen blocks, `U K` has four zero rows. A hybrid reader keeps the old cut on those rows and uses the inverse-transpose map on the four updated rows; a separate correction preserves the dirty baseline. Exact rational checks give `H^T d + C^T d = S^T d` and `H^T U K = S^T K`. The full hybrid has 225 coefficients, its correction has 152, and its net increase is 201 incidences over the original 176-add cut.

The selected cut precedes canonical phase `B`. For its exact state map `x_B = M_B x`, the verifier transports each centre readout as `A_post = M_B^-T A` and checks `M_B^T A_post = A` over all ordinary roles. The original cut becomes a 448-coefficient post-`B` reader on output ports. The retimed hybrid/correction supports and relaxed incidence-only sensitivities are:

| Fused tetrads | Hybrid support | Dirty correction | Added incidences vs. original | Incidence-only complex κ ceiling |
|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| 3 | 450 | 52 | 326 | 0.003212495586 |
| 5 | 454 | 76 | 354 | 0.007657155804 |
| 9 | 441 | 140 | 405 | 0.015679681607 |
| 14 | 437 | 215 | 476 | 0.024130777318 |

The original cut window after `A` and before `B` has a different frame profile: all 112 output roles and all eight active private centre accumulators are in frame 0, and the 176 source-bound cut ADDs use that same frame. A hybrid consumer kept at this pre-`B` boundary therefore needs no candidate frame joins for its added terms; its three-block incidence-only sensitivity remains `0.004947467105`. This is exact frame compatibility, not proof that the changed coefficients or separate dirty-baseline correction can be installed in the native schedule.

At the post-`B` boundary, the 112 output roles occupy distinct rank-8 frames, and the eight centre roles occupy frames 415–422. Their joint rank is 9 and their only common selected frame is frame 1. None of the 448 original retimed coefficients, nor the three-block hybrid/correction's 450/52 coefficients, is a direct same-frame ADD. The exact native checker validates 120 candidate rank-1 child recipes to bring these role frames to frame 1. Charging one common-frame pass lowers the 3/5/9/14-block sensitivities to 0.002797088144, 0.006698357356, 0.013825363860 and 0.021482998123, respectively.

These are optimistic planning sensitivities, not a scalar tariff, admitted supplier, proved schedule or achieved κ. For the three-block prefix, pre-`B` placement avoids the 120 post-`B` frame joins; the one-pass post-`B` profile excludes restoration and separate dirty-baseline execution. Adapter-expanded endpoint semantics, changed-cut installation, frame-value lifetimes, dirty-baseline availability, any duplicated `B` execution and the full bit-side invoice remain unproved. The selected κ remains `0.001672660197076918`; no frontier update or universal frame-join obstruction is claimed.

An exact source-side alternative avoids a separate dirty-baseline input. For the hybrid reader `H`, let `C=S-H` and `J=C^T U K`; then `S^T(d+UKx)-Jx=S^T(d+Kx)` on all fourteen pinned blocks. The correction supports are 64/96/192/288 for the 3/5/9/14-block prefixes, with incidence-only complex sensitivities 0.004756582174, 0.011073245628, 0.020601886496 and 0.029934752880. A separate exact completion census finds no unimodular four-kernel-row completion that preserves the original reader without correction: two blocks have an inconsistent zero-rank equation, two force rank-two quotient transfers, and the other ten have quotient determinant 2 (four blocks) or 16 (six blocks). This is scoped to the selected reader and route. The input source, schedule, frame/value lifetime and actual price for `Jx` remain unproved; no kappa improvement is claimed.

## Task and overlap

- Package: `research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer/`; PR tip: `30968c83f160011b5f435380746f0e57e64517d0`.
- Task: `coverage-law-change`, priority revision 6; scope **refined** to a source-bound P112 consumer audit of dirty-state corrections, pre-`B` placement and post-`B` retiming.
- Package source base: `b1ef0a5585418590320806c967383584c645132b`; canonical `main` at submission refresh: `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`.
- Exact input blobs and SHA-256 pins are recorded in `research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer/SOURCES.json`; selected-result SHA-256: `bb2eaa58647b353f88d0aec2eafb9d30df1be53589231b23e12ceef3e4bad129`.

Adjacent [PR #3344](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3344) screens larger-child and multiple-unpaid budgets; [PR #3566](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3566) binds the P112 decoder to selected ports; [PR #3567](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/pull/3567) screens a one-sided tetrad alphabet. This follow-up adds a source-bound inverse-transpose reader, exact native frame-join audit, input-side correction identity and route-scoped completion census; it makes no general novelty claim. The cached overlap scan covers 394 PRs and 2,319 discussions as of 2026-10-18 03:15 UTC, but refresh failed, so it is not a novelty certificate.

## Validation

Replayed with CPython 3.12:

```sh
python3.12 -B research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer/verify.py
python3.12 -B research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer/verify_input_correction.py
python3 scripts/research_package.py --package research/p112-tetrad-cut-consumer --check-only
git diff --check
```

The verifier pins the selected archive, program, native lift and exact Clifford child recipes. It checks the 176 native cut coefficients and chronology, reconstructs the fourteen tetrads, verifies the hybrid identities and dirty correction, audits pre-`B` common-frame labels, expands the canonical `B` map, checks inverse-transpose identities and prefix sensitivities, audits post-`B` role-frame labels, and exactly checks the 120 candidate rank-1 joins. A coefficient-mutation control rejects altered inputs. The separate exact checker reconstructs all fourteen J matrices, verifies the source-side identity and prefix sensitivities, and classifies the no-correction completion equations by exact rank, integrality and determinant. The package metadata and source pins pass their registered check. No changed native schedule, adapter-expanded implementation, physical scalar tariff, supplier admission or complete outer invoice is claimed.

## Credit

The P112 geometry, selected-port bijection, gauge44 word, native-lift recipes and bit-side price engine retain their predecessor attribution. This follow-up adds the hybrid dirty-state correction, exact canonical post-`B` readout maps, and native frame-join sensitivities, the source-side Jx correction and its scoped no-correction completion census. Prepared by Gonzalo Mier with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance; Apache-2.0.

## Open next questions

1. Can the three-block source correction Jx be produced at the native pre-B frame-0 cut from an admitted source and kept live through the centre readout? Bind one tetrad through the adapter-expanded provider and exact owner chronology, identify the source and frame/value lifetime for Jx, then price its scalar operations and cleanup. Its 64-coefficient incidence-only sensitivity is 0.004756582174, but source access, schedule and tariff remain unproved.
2. Does the complete joint scalar and bit-side invoice retain a kappa target above 0.003? Replace the rank-72 children and rank-1 incidence assumption with an admitted complex supplier and full native correction/restoration costs, then combine them with an independently admitted bit supplier. Neither supplier nor the full invoice is established.
